chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

There is no vigilance (ghayrah) in the lawful, following the words of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family): 'Do not do anything until I return to you both.' And when he returned to them, he placed his feet between them in the bedding.
ai.seo_question: What does the concept of Ghayrah mean in relation to Halal matters according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies that 'ghayrah' (protective jealousy) is not a mandatory religious obligation in lawful matters, distinguishing between natural affection and excessive possessiveness. The Prophet’s example of entering Ali and Fatimah’s private space by placing his feet between them illustrates that marital intimacy and familial closeness are inherently permissible without requiring constant vigilance or formal permission, a view supported by Shia jurists to encourage ease in family life.
